chapter: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
title: Singers George Dewey Washington and Walter Richardson
summary: They were the two most popular male singers in Chicago, moving between the Dreamland, Vendome, Metropolitan and Sunset.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now, I think that more or less covers it. Are there any other people you remember from that time, that maybe that I didn't bring up?
Well, I did mention George Dewey Washington and George Richardson, didn't I?

Well they were -- I thought I did. They were great singers. They were the two -- Walter Richardson. They were the two most popular male singers in Chicago at that time. And they sang at the Dreamland and they were singing at the Vendome Theater and Metropolitan Theater and other clubs, they'd go from club to club. Singing, maybe
a few days at the Sunset, a week a the Vendome. They were the two most popular male singers in Chicago at that time.
